about.title: McFarland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: McFarland sits along stretches of SR-99, Elmo Highway, Driver Road, and Garzoli Avenue that see a steady flow of local and through traffic, particularly on Wednesday mornings between 10 a.m. and noon when reported crashes tend to cluster. In a small city like this, even one serious collision can ripple through a family's daily routine. If you were hurt in a crash on these roads, the choices you make in the days afterward matter. What you say to an insurance adjuster, how quickly evidence is preserved, and whether you understand California's fault rules can all affect your ability to recover fair compensation. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly. Instead, we connect McFarland residents with independent personal injury attorneys who take cases on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless they recover money for you. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of understanding where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Talk to an Insurer

items.title: The Clock Starts Ticking Immediately
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but if a government entity (like a county road agency) is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early helps preserve your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible for the accident, though your share of fault reduces the amount. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault is argued fairly.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurance company may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, but you're not obligated to give one, and doing so without guidance can hurt your claim. An independent attorney can advise you before you say anything on the record.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in McFarland?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned road or vehicle, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible so no deadlines are missed.

items.question: Elmo Highway and SR-99 both run through McFarland. Does it matter where my accident happened?
items.answer: The specific road can affect who's responsible for maintenance and whether a government entity might be involved, which can change your filing deadline. It doesn't change your basic right to pursue compensation, but it's a detail worth mentioning when you speak with an attorney. Preserving photos, witness names, and location details early on can help clarify this later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so you can still seek compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your total recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't necessarily bar your claim entirely. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.
